lines: Phases 1 to 5 complete. Phase 6 in progress. The decision asked of Brandon in Status 236 at about 5:20 PM MT Friday stands unanswered: move on to the film and the masters, or one more round of looks first. The work goes on in either case and only the freeze waits. A second, smaller word will be asked of him once its pictures are drawn: whether to take the mend of spring's level line.

Film frame 2828, item 287, decision 290: the cause is named. Stated by the diagnosing builder at 1:58 AM MT Saturday as measured on its machine: it makes the odd bytes on purpose in two ways, the whole hash equal to the odd drawing's, by numbering the seasons' sets as if fall's had been made before winter's, and by holding winter's loads back by 400 ms with nothing else changed. On a page that captures, the four seasons are prepared at once and each set is made when its own loads end, and the drawing library draws solid things in the order they were numbered. So which load ends first can change one pixel. Not seen yet: a real odd drawing caught by the harness, and which two things tie at that pixel. Ruled: two idle machines are lent for the count until 3:00 AM MT, and the cure is ordered now on its own branch: the sets made in one order on every load, with the loads still side by side. Its floors: the usual drawing keeps its bytes, the eight guards equal the list, both forced forms give the usual bytes, and a test that fails on the main branch and passes with the cure. It is ordered before the catch because the masters are drawn in many browsers on a fast card, where loads may end in another order more often. Report due 3:40 AM MT, then chain 46.

Spring's level line, item 286, decision 289: the extended diagnosis is read whole and all nine of its sheets are looked at. Stated by the mender: with a straight ramp for the fade of the table's image in the glass, the largest change over 8 rows falls from 12.62 and 8.43 levels to 2.35 and 2.29, in the storm and at rest. Its cost as stated: 0.9 to 1.9 percent of a hero frame's pixels move in all four seasons by 0.7 to 1.9 levels in the mean, so all eight guards move; a light of the room shows as a small bright oval and a thin streak; summer misses two of the aims by under one level; a frame costs the same time. Seen by me in the second picture attached: the level edge left of the chimney on the main branch, none with the candidate. Looked at here: the four approved pictures at that place show no level line. Ruled: nothing is merged. The candidate is made ready and proven on a held branch, so that a yes lands in one step and a no costs nothing: motion on the live page, the other seasons, the two small lights, film frames, and 4K frames at the masters' tier. Report due 3:15 AM MT, then before and after pictures with the ask. New item 288: with the table's image, rows of winter's live frame below the switch are darker by 4.6 to 9.6 levels, cause to be found.

The render instructions for his own computer, decision 287: the hosted run on the newest head cb184536 is complete with all ten jobs passed, measured at 1:50 AM MT. But one path through the instructions could draw every frame and end with no film. Read here in the code: the one byte for byte check is a small calibration picture, every chunk of the film names its hash, the short test drew it anew each time, and the join refuses two hashes. Measured by the builder: on the hosted Mac 8 drawings gave 8 different hashes, on hosted Windows 20 drawings gave one. The mend is ordered with proof by run on both. So the instructions reach him later than said: the builder's last report is due by 3:50 AM MT, then the merge, a cold read by a fresh critic and the one line for Claude Code. No final render is started in the cloud.

The first shake's mend, decision 288: it costs no load time. Stated by the helper: four pairs of loads, the main branch 161,189 ms in the mean and the mend 158,618 ms. Inside the first shake the stand falls from 5,684 to 5,753 ms to 64 to 74 ms. What remains: a stand of 3.9 to 5.5 s right after the first picture on a software renderer; on a real graphics card unknown.

Chain 45's two 4K frames at the masters' tier are in and equal their expected bytes: film frame 620, winter's frost, and film frame 1470, summer's lights. A slip of mine is logged with it: my order named the wrong tool for frame 1470, so its first drawing could not equal the value I gave. Drawn again with the masters' own tool it is equal, stated by the helper; and measured here, the first drawing equals its own counterpart byte for byte. Seen by me in the first and third picture attached: summer half a second after its landing at 4K, the seeds as whole soft smears, the lights as thin streaks, no rows of dots, nothing torn.

Under way. The sixteenth publish is begun: a helper draws the page's first pictures on the landed tree, then the build, the security review and a live check that counts the stand inside each shake, then it goes live with the first shake's mend, the frost and the slim lights. The strips for the change critic: the whole film sheet is in, four more are due by 2:15 AM MT, then a fresh critic. The second form of the counter of broken samples: its floors are met so far as stated by its builder, report by 3:30 AM MT.

Remaining in phase 6 and what he receives. The sixteenth publish on the live page. The render instructions: one file in the repo and one line to give Claude Code. On his word the freeze: the repo goes private and the references are redrawn. Then the film steps of the build order and the full 4K 60 render on his gaming PC on his word: With Prompt and Without Prompt at 3840x2160, the Portfolio Looping Video and the Portfolio Screenshot. Last, a fresh reviewer's score against the showcase standard and BUILD COMPLETE. Open, below the bar, as in Status 255 with two changes: film frame 2828's cause is named and its cure ordered, and item 288 is new. Not verified: a real graphics card, a phone, Safari, Firefox, sound heard by a person.
Sound credits 7,420 of 10,000 (measured from the ledger at 2:01 AM MT: 52 calls), no call since 05:47 UTC on Thursday (10:47 PM MT Wednesday). No film render and no new preview since Preview 07.
